t: Right — the coursebook. Peter, you had the strongest view last time, so start us off.

My view has not changed. Unit seven is too long for the hours we have. Eighteen hours, twenty on paper, and either way the writing gets cut. I would drop the second reading text and give that time back to the writing.
I would keep the second text. It is the only place where they read two sources against each other, and that is the thing they actually cannot do yet.
They cannot do it in twenty minutes either. That is my point. Half of them do not finish it.
So we agree the unit is too long. We disagree about which part goes.
I am not sure we agree it is too long. It is too long the way it is currently sequenced. If the second text moved to the start of the unit, it would have the whole unit behind it.
That is a different proposal, and it is a better one than mine, honestly. But it changes the plan document, not just the timing.
It does. And the plan document is the one the teachers actually use, so that is a real cost. Rachel, how long would the resequencing take?
To write? An afternoon. To get it approved? That I cannot tell you.
Fine. Then let us take it as a proposal, not a decision. Anything else on the coursebook before we move on?
